Add the Living Kidney Donor Profile Index

Source: R/add_lkdpi.R
add_lkdpi.Rd

Computes the Living Kidney Donor Profile Index (LKDPI) for living donor kidney transplants and appends it (default column LKDPI). The LKDPI is on the same scale as the deceased donor KDPI, but it is not limited to 0-100: a negative value means less risk than any deceased donor kidney in the reference population.

Usage

add_lkdpi(
  df,
  creatinine = "DON_KI_CREAT_PREOP",
  egfr_equation = c("ckd_epi_2009", "ckd_epi_2021"),
  a2_donor = c("incompatible", "compatible"),
  lkdpi_col = "LKDPI",
  return_terms = FALSE
)

Arguments

df

A data frame of living donor kidney transplants, one row each.

creatinine

Name of the donor creatinine column used for eGFR. Defaults to "DON_KI_CREAT_PREOP" (pre-donation creatinine), a convention.

egfr_equation

eGFR equation passed to add_donor_egfr(). "ckd_epi_2009" (default) is the CKD-EPI equation the paper used. "ckd_epi_2021" is the newer equation without race; the coefficients were not fit with it.

a2_donor

Whether an A2 or A2B donor counts as ABO incompatible with a recipient lacking the A antigen. "incompatible" (default) follows the antigens; "compatible" treats A2 as lacking A, as in A2-to-B allocation. Both are conventions; the paper does not say.

lkdpi_col

Name of the output column.

return_terms

If TRUE, also add a list-column LKDPI_terms with each row's components.

Value

df with a new column.

Details

The inputs come from both the living donor file (DONOR_LIVE) and the kidney transplant file (TX_KI), so join them first:

FactorColumns
Donor ageDON_AGE
Donor eGFRcomputed with add_donor_egfr() from creatinine, DON_AGE, DON_GENDER and race
Donor BMIDON_WGT_KG, DON_HGT_CM
Donor African AmericanDON_RACE_BLACK_AFRICAN_AMERICAN (Y/N), or DON_RACE = 16 (1024 = unknown)
Donor cigarette useDON_HIST_CIGARETTE (Y/N)
Donor systolic blood pressureDON_BP_PREOP_SYST
Male donor to male recipientDON_GENDER, CAN_GENDER
ABO incompatibleDON_ABO, CAN_ABO
Unrelated donorDON_RELATIONSHIP_TY
HLA-B and HLA-DR mismatchesREC_B_MM_EQUIV_TX, REC_DR_MM_EQUIV_TX
Donor/recipient weight ratioDON_WGT_KG, REC_WGT_KG

The paper states its factors but not how each was read from SRTR fields. The mapping above, and these rules, are this package's reading:

  • ABO incompatible means the donor carries an A or B antigen the recipient lacks (A, A1 and A2 carry A; AB, A1B and A2B carry both).

  • Unrelated means a non-biological relationship: codes 7 to 12, 15 and 999 of format LVDNRL.

References

Massie AB, Leanza J, Fahmy LM, et al. A risk index for living donor kidney transplantation. Am J Transplant 2016;16:2077-2084. doi:10.1111/ajt.13709 (Results, "Calculation of the LKDPI".)

Examples

pairs <- data.frame(
  DON_AGE = 60, DON_GENDER = "M", CAN_GENDER = "M",
  DON_HGT_CM = 180, DON_WGT_KG = 90, REC_WGT_KG = 80,
  DON_KI_CREAT_PREOP = 1.0, DON_RACE = 8, DON_HIST_CIGARETTE = "N",
  DON_BP_PREOP_SYST = 125, DON_ABO = "O", CAN_ABO = "A",
  DON_RELATIONSHIP_TY = 4, REC_B_MM_EQUIV_TX = 1, REC_DR_MM_EQUIV_TX = 1
)
add_lkdpi(pairs)
#>   DON_AGE DON_GENDER CAN_GENDER DON_HGT_CM DON_WGT_KG REC_WGT_KG
#> 1      60          M          M        180         90         80
#>   DON_KI_CREAT_PREOP DON_RACE DON_HIST_CIGARETTE DON_BP_PREOP_SYST DON_ABO
#> 1                  1        8                  N               125       O
#>   CAN_ABO DON_RELATIONSHIP_TY REC_B_MM_EQUIV_TX REC_DR_MM_EQUIV_TX    LKDPI
#> 1       A                   4                 1                  1 13.22419
